message.content: A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **syncytium** (plural: syncytia). Syncytia are formed when several cells fuse together, resulting in a single large cell with multiple nuclei. Examples include certain muscle cells (e.g., skeletal muscle fibers) and osteoclasts (bone‑resorbing cells).
